dimensions.headline: fits fires on 94.5% of hits vs 84% of controls — a statistically non-null but sub-threshold 11-point gap (OR 3.17) that collapses to INCONCLUSIVE once leaked rows are removed.
dimensions.findings: The blind primary 2x2 shows p_hit=0.945 (CI 0.886–0.975) vs p_ctrl=0.840 (CI 0.745–0.904), giving risk_difference=0.106 (11 pts, RD CI 0.015–0.196) and odds_ratio=3.168 (OR CI 1.184–8.477). Both the RD CI and the OR CI exclude the null, so a directional association is present — but the effect is only 11 points, below the pre-registered 15-point materiality bar, and the risk_ratio is a modest 1.126; hence the stated verdict INCONCLUSIVE (RD<15pt). The significance is fragile: with a 47% leak_rate, the no-leak subset gives RD=0.073 (7 pts, CI −0.046 to 0.192, OR 2.719 CI 0.63–11.73) and the high-confidence subset gives RD=0.086 (9 pts, CI −0.002 to 0.175, OR 2.739 CI 0.998–7.52) — both CIs cross zero/one, so the apparent separation is INCONCLUSIVE and is carried substantially by leaked rows. Why the top-line contrast is weak is explained by a ceiling/composition effect: controls are dominated by the moderate band (50 of 81, plus 25 modest, only 6 flop), and moderate controls already fit at 90% and modest at 84%, leaving little headroom above the 95% hit rate. Yet the underlying signal is real as a gradient — the band ladder rises monotonically flop 33% → modest 84% → moderate 90% → hit 95%, with Cochran-Armitage z=3.87 (p≈0, monotone_increasing=true). So fits tracks commercial tier in a dose-response sense but does NOT cleanly discriminate 1M+ hits from well-matched near-miss controls at the top of the scale. Separately, a confirmation-bias flag: blind coding rated 95% of hits as fitting vs 55% under the original unblinded pass (42% disagreement), so the blind fits rate itself may be inflated.
dimensions.caveats: Observational and matched, not randomized — association only, no causal claim. The full-sample RD CI (0.015–0.196) technically excludes zero, but it is not "no difference" nor a clean positive: it is INCONCLUSIVE because RD=11pts is below the 15-pt bar AND both leak-robustness subsets have CIs spanning zero. The 47% leak rate is high, and results depend materially on leaked rows. A ceiling effect (controls concentrated in the moderate band, already ~90% fitting) mechanically compresses the top-tier contrast, so a weak hit-vs-control gap does not imply the construct is inert — the monotone band trend argues the opposite. The 42% blind-vs-original disagreement and 95% blind fit rate suggest the blind fits label may be over-inclusive, which would further shrink true discrimination. n_controls=81 (only 6 flops) limits power at the low end.

dimensions.headline: Fits-rate rises monotonically flop→modest→moderate→hit (33→84→90→95%, Cochran-Armitage z=3.87, p≈0), but the trend is driven almost entirely by the tiny n=6 flop cell — above flop the gradient is nearly flat and saturating.
dimensions.findings: The blind "fits" rate increases at every step of the ordinal success ladder: flop 2/6=33%, modest 21/25=84%, moderate 45/50=90%, hit 104/110=95%. The Cochran-Armitage trend test (scores 0/1/2/3) gives z=3.87, p≈0, monotone_increasing=true — so a strictly ordered, statistically significant positive trend is present and not an artifact of collapsing bands. However, the trend is structurally lopsided: the flop→modest step is +51 points (33→84%), whereas modest→moderate→hit together add only +11 points (84→90→95%) and are consistent with a ceiling/saturation pattern. Because the flop cell is only n=6 (k=2), a single reclassification there swings its rate by ~17 points, so the CA statistic leans heavily on 6 observations. Above the flop band the three upper cells (n=25/50/110) are near-ceiling and only weakly separable; the effective discrimination is flop-vs-everything-else, not a smooth four-level dose-response. This gradient should also be read against the primary hit-vs-control contrast, which is INCONCLUSIVE (RD=10.6pts, 95% CI [1.5, 19.6]; RD<15pt threshold; OR=3.17, CI [1.18, 8.48]) and degrades further under leak-adjustment (leak rate 47%; no-leak RD=7pts, CI [-4.6, 19.2], INCONCLUSIVE; hi-confidence RD=9pts, CI [-0.2, 17.5], INCONCLUSIVE). Note the gradient is partly tautological: bands are defined by commercial outcome and "fits" is a rubric judgment about whether the design-DNA matches the success thesis, so higher bands are expected to fit more by construction.

dimensions.caveats: Observational and blind-coded — association, not causation. The CA trend is real and monotone but leans on the n=6 flop cell; the top three bands are near-ceiling (84/90/95%) and only weakly separable, so this is effectively "flop vs rest," not a smooth 4-level dose-response. Bands are outcome-defined and "fits" is a thesis-conformity judgment, making the gradient partly circular. Confirmation-bias signal is large: blind fits 95% vs original unblinded 55%, with 42% blind-vs-original disagreement, so the absolute fits levels are label-sensitive. The overall hit-vs-control effect is INCONCLUSIVE (RD 10.6pt <15pt; weakens to 7–9pt with CIs crossing zero under 47% leak adjustment), so the gradient does not establish a powered hit-vs-control difference.

dimensions.headline: Only the novelty gate (max_novelty>=3) does any separating work (RD +12pt, OR 3.78) — but even it is INCONCLUSIVE; the familiarity and twist gates are saturated in BOTH arms and separate nothing.
dimensions.findings: The 3-gate fits composite decomposes cleanly into one live gate and two dead ones. (1) familiarity>=3: hit 99% vs ctrl 99%, RD 0pt, OR 1.36 — essentially every game in both arms clears it, so it carries zero discriminative signal (a near-universal precondition, not a hit differentiator). (2) twist_present: hit 100% vs ctrl 96%, RD only 4pt; the OR of 9.854 looks dramatic but is an artifact of a near-ceiling contrast (100 vs 96 — the "10x odds" reflects that hits have literally zero twist-absent cases, i.e. a 0-cell, not a large practical gap). Both arms are twist-saturated. (3) max_novelty>=3: hit 96% vs ctrl 84%, RD +12pt, OR 3.78 — this is the ONLY gate with a real between-arm gap, and it single-handedly accounts for essentially all of the composite fits signal (primary blind RD is +11pt; the novelty gate's +12pt tracks it almost exactly). So "does the design clear the fits bar" reduces operationally to "does it reach novelty>=3." Crucially, at RD +12pt the novelty gate still sits under the study's own 15pt powered threshold, so it must be read as INCONCLUSIVE, not established. Corroborating the novelty axis as the load-bearing one: in the ranked feature table novelty>=4 is itself a positive discriminator (65% vs 52%, RD +13pt, OR 1.68), and the band gradient is monotone increasing (flop 33% -> modest 84% -> moderate 90% -> hit 95% fits; Cochran-Armitage z=3.87). Note the two dead gates are dead for opposite reasons: familiarity is a floor both arms already stand on, while twist is a ceiling both arms already hit.

rows.read: near-ceiling both arms; OR inflated by 0-cell; INCONCLUSIVE
only real separator, but RD<15 -> INCONCLUSIVE

dimensions.caveats: Observational, matched design — association not causation. No per-gate confidence intervals were supplied, so significance for the three gate contrasts cannot be tested directly; however all three RDs (0, 4, 12pt) fall below the study's stated 15pt powered threshold, so NONE is individually established — the novelty gate is the strongest candidate but remains INCONCLUSIVE. The twist gate's OR of 9.854 is not trustworthy as an effect size: it derives from a 100%-vs-96% contrast with a zero cell (no twist-absent hits), which explodes the odds ratio while the actual RD is only 4pt. Both familiarity and twist are near-universal (>=96%) in controls too, meaning these gates describe a baseline of what shipped games look like in this window, not what makes a hit. Confidence-bias flag is severe: blind fits 95% vs original unblinded 55% (42% disagreement), so absolute fit rates are coder-dependent even if between-arm gaps are less so. Sensitivity analyses on the overall composite (leak-adjusted RD +7pt, hi-confidence RD +9pt, both CIs crossing zero) reinforce that the whole fits signal is fragile — and since the composite signal is essentially the novelty gate, that fragility applies directly to the one gate that separates. Small control tail (flop n=6) makes the low end of the gradient noisy.

dimensions.headline: What separates hits is production-scale (price $20+, teams >5, co-op) plus a few twist types (co-op-social, roguelike, scope-disruption) — NOT the ubiquitous twists (mechanical_swap, aesthetic_reframe) that both arms share equally.
dimensions.caveats: Association only, observational — not causation. (1) The feature table reports point RD/OR with NO per-feature confidence intervals, so individual "separators" are unhedged; treat the ~15pt cutoff as a rough eyeball, not a significance test. (2) ~19 features were scanned with no multiple-comparisons correction — expect 1-2 false positives among the borderline (14-18pt) rows. (3) Heavy collinearity: price<$20, team<=5/solo, and co_op all proxy the same latent "production scale/budget," so they are not four independent findings but largely one — the co_op / co_op_social_layer pair likewise double-counts. (4) The price and team directions plausibly reflect SURVIVORSHIP (1M+ sellers are bigger games because scale buys marketing/polish) rather than a design lever a small studio can pull. (5) The overall primary contrast is itself underpowered and INCONCLUSIVE (blind RD 11pt, CI [1.5,19.6]; leak-sensitivity RD drops to 7pt, CI crosses zero [-4.6,19.2]) with a 47% leak rate, so feature-level gaps sit atop a weak base signal. (6) Confirmation-bias flag: blind fits 95% vs original-unblinded 55% (42% disagreement) means the coded "twist" features carry rater latitude. (7) n_controls=81 is band-skewed (50 moderate / 25 modest / 6 flop), so "control" here means mostly moderate-success games, compressing hit-vs-control contrasts.

dimensions.headline: Blind coding rated 95% of hits as "fits" vs 55% unblinded (+40pt), with 42% of hits flipping between passes — the gap runs opposite to theory-confirming bias and mostly signals a lenient, noisy rubric.
dimensions.findings: On the same 110 hits, the blind pass coded 95% as fitting the theory (blind_fits_pct=95) versus 55% in the phase-1 unblinded pass (original_unblinded_fits_pct=55) — a +40 point delta — and the two passes disagreed on 42% of individual hits (blind_vs_orig_disagreement_pct=42). The direction is diagnostically important: naive confirmation bias predicts the UNBLINDED rate should be inflated (coders who know a title is a hit talk themselves into "fits"), which would make unblinded > blind. Here the opposite holds — blind is 40pts HIGHER — so the pattern is not theory-confirming inflation of the unblinded pass; instead the blind rubric is markedly more lenient/generous than the original human judgment. The 42% disagreement is near coin-flip magnitude and, since only ~5% of hits are blind-"no", almost all of that disagreement is one-directional: cases the unblinded pass called "no" the blind pass reclassifies as "fits." This means most of the delta is rubric drift + coding noise, not a clean bias signal, and the blind 95% sits at a near-ceiling that barely discriminates hits from the control arm (p_ctrl=0.84; blind primary RD=10.6pts, rd_ci [1.5, 19.6], OR=3.168 [1.184, 8.477], verdict INCONCLUSIVE because RD<15pt). Under leak-adjusted sensitivity the separation weakens further and the CI crosses zero (no-leak RD=7pts, rd_ci [-4.6, 19.2], OR=2.719 [0.63, 11.73] — INCONCLUSIVE), so the residual hit-vs-control edge is not robust to a 47% leak rate. Net: the blind fits-rate is high but this is driven by a permissive rubric that says "fits" for almost any familiar-base + twist design (the band gradient rises 33/84/90/95 across flop/modest/moderate/hit, Cochran-Armitage z=3.87, monotone), and the 40pt blind-vs-unblinded gap plus 42% disagreement should be read as an inter-pass reliability problem (rubric leniency and noise), not as evidence of confirmation bias operating in the expected direction.

dimensions.caveats: Observational and association-only; no causal claim. The confirmation_bias block gives only aggregate rates (95% vs 55%, 42% disagreement) — the raw phase-1 unblinded per-title codes are not in the sample rows, so I cannot verify the directionality of each disagreement or compute a kappa; the "mostly one-directional" inference rests on the near-ceiling blind rate leaving little room for blind-"no" flips. "Unblinded" and "blind" may differ in rubric version and coder, so the 40pt gap conflates rubric change with blinding. The blind hit-vs-control contrasts are underpowered (powered=false) and INCONCLUSIVE under both the primary and leak-adjusted specs (RD<15pt and/or CI crossing zero), so the blind pass's ability to separate hits from controls is not established regardless of the bias interpretation. Leak rate is high (47%), and leaked design-DNA could itself inflate the blind fits-rate.

dimensions.headline: "Familiar base + twist" is necessary-not-sufficient — near-universal in BOTH arms (base gate RD 0pts), so it is a floor condition, not a hit discriminator; what actually separates bands is the DEGREE and FLAVOR of novelty.
dimensions.findings: The compound pattern does not cleanly discriminate hits from comparable non-hits. The full blind "fits" rubric is 94.5% in hits vs 84.0% in controls: RD = 10.6pts (CI [1.5, 19.6]), OR = 3.17 (CI [1.18, 8.48]) — the study's own verdict is INCONCLUSIVE because RD < 15pts, even though the CI just excludes zero. Decomposing the gate shows WHY it fails as a discriminator: the "familiar base" leg (familiarity>=3) is 99% in hits AND 99% in controls (RD 0pts, OR 1.36 — non-discriminating), and "twist_present" is 100% vs 96% (RD only 4pts). Both legs are effectively saturated in both arms, so a game HAVING a familiar base and a twist tells you almost nothing about whether it hit — it is table stakes. The discriminating margin lives entirely in the third leg, max_novelty>=3: 96% vs 84%, RD 12pts, OR 3.78 — i.e. it is not the PRESENCE of a twist but its AMBITION/execution that shifts the odds, and even that is only 12pts. This is reinforced by a genuine dose-response: fit rate climbs monotonically 33% (flop, n=6) → 84% (modest) → 90% (moderate) → 95% (hit), Cochran-Armitage z = 3.87 (p ≈ 0, monotone increasing) — the pattern tracks the success ladder continuously rather than switching on at "hit," which is the signature of a necessary-not-sufficient quality gradient. Robustness cuts against a strong claim: removing the ~47% leaked rows drops RD to 7pts (CI [-4.6, 19.2], crosses zero, INCONCLUSIVE) and the high-confidence-only subset gives RD 9pts (CI [-0.2, 17.5], crosses zero, INCONCLUSIVE) — so the headline 11pt gap is not robust to de-leaking or confidence restriction. Finally, confirmation-bias telemetry is decisive for the honest claim: blind coders saw the pattern in 95% of hits vs only 55% under the original UN-blinded pass (42% disagreement) — the rubric finds "familiar base + twist" nearly everywhere once you look for it, which is itself evidence of non-discrimination, not of a hit formula. Where real separation exists it is in specific ingredients, not the abstract pattern: co_op (58% vs 33%, RD +25, OR 2.75), twist:co_op_social_layer (47% vs 26%, RD +21), twist:procedural_roguelike_layer (25% vs 7%, RD +17, OR 3.83), higher price tier (price<$20 is NEGATIVE: 31% vs 59%, RD -28, OR 0.31), and familiarity>=4 (56% vs 37%, RD +18) — while generic twists like mechanical_swap (67% vs 69%, RD -2) and aesthetic_reframe (59% vs 68%, RD -9) do not discriminate at all. Honest revised claim: "familiar base + twist" is a NECESSARY-NOT-SUFFICIENT entry condition (near-universal among viable releases in both arms; base-familiarity leg is outright non-discriminating at RD 0), NOT a hit predictor. It functions as a floor you must clear, not a lever that separates hits from equally-twisted non-hits.

tables.title: Gate decomposition — which leg actually discriminates
Sensitivity — headline gap is not robust

dimensions.caveats: Observational and association-only — controls were selected to be COMPARABLE releases, which by construction pushes the base pattern toward saturation in both arms (a restriction/selection effect); a random no-name control pool would likely show a larger base-familiarity gap, so "non-discriminating" is conditional on the matched design. The primary contrast is underpowered (study flags powered=false) and its own verdict is INCONCLUSIVE at RD 10.6pts; de-leaking (leak rate 47%) and confidence-restriction both push RD below significance with CIs crossing zero, so do not read the 11pt gap as established. flop band n=6 makes the low end of the gradient fragile. The feature-discrimination and twist-type percentages are descriptive, uncorrected for multiple comparisons, and several ORs have wide/unreported CIs — treat co_op, roguelike-layer, price-tier signals as hypotheses, not confirmed effects. The 42% blind-vs-unblinded disagreement indicates the rubric is susceptible to post-hoc pattern-seeing; the blind numbers are the trustworthy ones and they are what show near-universality.

redteam_ko:
방어 논리에 대한 가장 강한 정직한 반박(한국어):

이 연구의 핵심 신호는 통제집단 설계에 의해 사실상 만들어졌을 수 있다. 첫째, "적격성 필터"가 이미 familiarity≥3 게이트(hit 99% vs ctrl 99%, RD 0pt)와 twist_present(hit 100% vs ctrl 96%, RD 4pt)를 양쪽 모두 통과하도록 통제집단을 선별했다면, 남는 판별력의 대부분은 진짜 인과가 아니라 밴드 배정 규칙과 표본 구성의 산물이며, 실제로 flop 밴드는 n=6·k=2에 불과해 33% 수치는 통계적으로 무의미하고 단조증가 추세(z=3.87) 자체가 소수의 극단 셀에 의존한다. 둘째, 정보 가용성 비대칭이 결정적이다. 히트작은 문서화가 풍부해 twist를 코더가 쉽게 "발견"하는 반면 비히트작은 자료가 빈약해 twist가 실재해도 누락되는데, 이는 confirmation_bias 지표에서 그대로 드러난다. 블라인드 적합률 95%가 원저자의 비블라인드 55%와 42%나 불일치한다는 것은 코딩이 결과를 알수록 twist를 더 많이 붙였다는 방향성 오염의 직접 증거다. 셋째, 이 코딩 잡음은 오히려 귀무가설 쪽으로의 감쇠(attenuation-toward-null)를 일으키므로, "차이 없음"이라는 결론조차 진짜 효과의 부재가 아니라 측정 오차로 상당 부분 설명될 수 있어 어느 방향으로도 결론을 내릴 수 없다. 넷째, 감도분석이 이를 확증한다. 누출률이 47%에 달하고 누출을 제거하면 RD가 10.6pt에서 7.3pt로 떨어지며 신뢰구간 [-0.046, 0.192]와 OR 신뢰구간 [0.63, 11.729]이 모두 무효값(0과 1)을 가로질러, 1차 분석의 "유의성"(OR 3.168, CI [1.184, 8.477])이 누출된 관측치에 의존하고 있음을 보여준다 — 즉 검정력 미달(powered:false)과 RD<15pt로 판정 자체가 INCONCLUSIVE다. 다섯째, 설령 차이가 실재해도 마케팅 예산·위시리스트 축적·출시 타이밍·순수한 운 같은 미측정 교란요인이 통제되지 않았고, price<$20가 오히려 통제집단에 유리한(RD -28pt) 등 특징들이 서로 얽혀 있어 "친숙한 기반+참신한 변주"는 히트의 원인이 아니라 잘 문서화된 성공작에 사후적으로 붙는 상관 서술일 뿐이다 — 이는 인과가 아니라 연관이며, 그것도 취약한 연관이다.
critic_ko: 통제군의 최대 취약점은 flop 밴드(n=6)로, 이 셀만으로는 저성과 구간의 적합률 추정이 사실상 불가능하며 modest(25)·moderate(50)도 밴드별 회귀에는 얇습니다. 또한 licensed_IP, input_embodiment, physics_jank_emergence, price_or_scope_disruption 같은 저빈도 twist 피처는 양쪽 표본이 한 자릿수 %라 개별 OR이 불안정하고, 통제군(81)이 히트(110)보다 적어 primary 2x2가 이미 미검정(powered:false, RD<15pt)인 상태입니다. 결정적으로 leak_rate 47%에 누수 제거 시 RD가 11→7pt로 무너지고 CI가 0을 포함하며, blind 대 원본 적합률 괴리(95% vs 55%, 불일치 42%)는 확증편향 위험을 시사합니다. 강화하려면 flop/modest 밴드와 통제군 표본을 대폭 늘려 밴드당 최소 수십 개를 확보하고, 누수 없는 하이컨피던스 하위표본만으로 사전등록된 코딩 기준에 따라 재검정하며, 저빈도 twist는 상위 카테고리로 묶어 검정력을 확보하는 것이 필요합니다.
